extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers interested in heroic character, literary criticism, and moral-philosophical qualities of writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for representing and judging heroic figures and religious/poetic texts, emphasizing inner sincerity, depth of vision, and lived conviction over formal schooling or polished craft. Applicable to writers aiming to render convincing, morally serious protagonists and to critics evaluating the authenticity and power of such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking through the shows of things into things
rubrics_metrics.description: A Hero ... looks through the shows of things into things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The heroic temperament is defined by its ability to see beyond custom, hearsay, and respectable formulas to the underlying Reality. Use and wont, respectable hearsay, and popular idolatries are treated as surface; the hero must perceive and answer the deeper truth. In characterization, show protagonists who probe beyond appearances and confront fundamental questions (What am I? What is Life?). This depth of vision is the Alpha and Omega of heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity of vision and heart
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincerity ... seems to me the merit of the Koran; the first and last merit in a book. The test of a sincere heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize authentic conviction in a character's beliefs and in the author's voice. Sincerity can outweigh literary polish: a work 'come from the heart' will reach other hearts even if rough. In depicting prophetic or heroic figures, emphasize inward earnestness, truthfulness of motive, and a voice that feels direct from the 'great Heart of Nature.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuineness / bona-fide quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary character of the Koran is this of its genuineness, of its being a bona-fide book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity of origin (the sense that the material issues from a real, deeply-felt source) is crucial. The presence of a genuine core—'wheat'—matters far more than formal refinement. Even chaotic or uncultivated expression is valuable if it embodies a real soul at work; critics should distinguish between mere artifice and genuine inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heart over craft (emotional truth over author-craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book come from the heart, it will contrive to reach other hearts; all art and author-craft are of small amount to that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional power and authenticity trump technical perfection. Writers should not let concerns about style or strict method extinguish the living passion behind the work. For critics, assess whether the work communicates a living conviction rather than merely exhibiting polished technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of a core truth (wheat vs chaff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not how much chaff is in you; but whether you have any wheat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating writing, look for a genuine, central truth or insight. Superfluous, repetitive, or crude material can be tolerated if a living truth is present. The 'soul of truth' determines a work's lasting value more than surface purity or absence of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passionate intensity and urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: The panting breathless haste and vehemence of a man struggling in the thick of battle for life and salvation; a headlong haste; for very magnitude of meaning he cannot get himself articulated into words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensity of conviction and urgency in expression are virtues even when they produce disorderly or inarticulate prose. Portrayals that capture a character's compelling urgency and inner turmoil can be more convincing than calm, measured exposition. Allow for rhapsodic, repetitive, or abrupt phrasing if it reflects genuine fervor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lived experience over formal schooling
rubrics_metrics.description: He had no school-learning; Life in the Desert, with its experiences, was all his education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-world experience and intimate familiarity with life can supply insight and authority that formal education cannot. In creating heroes or prophets, emphasize formative lived experiences and sensory acquaintance with the world as sources of credibility and vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence and polished order are subordinate to truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The thoughts crowd on him pell-mell: for very multitude of things to say, he can get nothing said. The meaning that is in him shapes itself into no form of composition, is stated in no sequence, method, or coherence;--they are not shaped at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disorder, iteration, and lack of literary method are not necessarily defects if they reflect a genuine inner pressure to express. Critics and writers should recognize when ragged structure embodies urgency and sincerity; historical sequence or tidy composition may be less important than preserving the authentic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directness of perception / 'sincerity of vision'
rubrics_metrics.description: The eye that flashes direct into the heart of things, and sees the truth of them ... sincerity of vision; the test of a sincere heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuate writing that displays immediate, unmediated insight into human and natural facts. Concrete, first-hand glimpses—rather than abstract dialectics—demonstrate a creator's honest engagement with reality. Show, through specific images and observations, an author's or character's direct apprehension of the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natural, concrete 'signs' and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Look over the world, says he; is it not wonderful, the work of Allah; wholly 'a sign to you' ... The clouds ... rain-deluges 'to revive a dead earth' ... Ships ... Huge moving mountains ... Ye have compassion on one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ vivid natural images and everyday phenomena as signs and evidence of larger truths; this grounds abstract claims and makes persuasion tangible. In character or sermon-writing, concrete examples from nature and common life lend plausibility and rhetorical force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral motive and non-ambitious authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: All his 'ambition,' seemingly, had been, hitherto, to live an honest life ... Not till he was already getting old ... did he start on the 'career of ambition;' and, belying all his past character ... set up as a wretched empty charlatan ... I have no faith whatever in that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a heroic figure, examine motive: authentic moral conviction (not personal ambition or gain) is a key indicator of true heroism. Writers should make motives evident through consistent past conduct and inward seriousness; critics should treat sudden, unexplained shifts to worldly ambition with skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to struggle and defend beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Driven foully out of his native country ... the wild Son of the Desert resolved to defend himself, like a man and Arab. If the Koreish will have it so, they shall have it. Tidings ... they would trample them down by sheer violence, steel and murder: well, let steel try it then!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heroism includes active defense of convictions, including readiness to endure hardship or conflict. In narrative, show the protagonist's struggle—flight, exile, battles—as part of their credibility. Evaluations should allow that new movements may propagate by many means; willingness to fight does not by itself disqualify truth.
